newsitem.title: USA: Apache Seagull confirm Egyptian find.
newsitem.headline: Apache Seagull confirm Egyptian find.

text.p: Apache Corp said Tuesday its Wadi El Rayan-5X appraisal well has confirmed the existence of a new oil field on the Qarun Concession in Egypt.
Early production from the oil field, the southernmost in the Western Desert, is expected to be transported by truck, beginning this summer.
Apache owns a 75 percent contractor interest in the concession and is operator. Houston based Seagull Energy Corp owns the remaining 25 percent.
The Wadi El Rayan-5X tested at a daily rate of 1,764 barrels of 26-degree gravity oil from 85 feet of net pay.
The well was tested using a a one-inch choke with 40 pounds per square inch of flowing tubing pressure. Perforations were between 5,630 feet and 5,732 feet in the Abu Roash "G" Cretaceous sandstone.

Additional drilling is planned to delineate the extent of the reservoir, Apache said. A 366,000-acre development lease has been established to pursue additional prospects identified along the Wadi El Rayan trend.

The 5X is the appraisal well for the Wadi El Rayan-1X discovery, which was completed last fall. The new field is located about 35 miles south of the nearest production and about a mile north of the 6.8-million-acre East Beni Suef Concession, where Apache and Seagull each have a 50 percent interest and plan two exploratory wells for later this year.
